neighbours.label: Pushback clause after a sentence-opening contrast marker: once 'But' / 'However' / 'Yet' opens a sentence that cautions or concedes against what was just said, the pole fires on the next early word ('But don't⟦ let⟧…', 'However, even⟦ though⟧…', 'However, don't⟦ assume⟧…'). The same words (let, though, whether) without the contrast opener stay quiet.
fire: The forecast looks grim for the weekend. But don't let a little rain keep you away from the parade.
The application form runs to twelve pages. However, don't let the paperwork discourage you from applying.
Critics panned the sequel when it came out. But don't assume the whole series is a waste of your evening.
The museum is small and easy to miss. However, even though the building is modest, the collection is superb.
Sales dipped again in the third quarter. Yet whether the slump will last is far from certain.
The recipe has more than twenty ingredients. But don't let the long list put you off trying it.
The hike gains a thousand metres in altitude. Still, just because a route is hard does not make it dangerous.
The laptop is heavier than its rivals. But do not allow the extra weight to decide the matter for you.
quiet: The forecast looks grim for the weekend. We will let the children decide about the parade.
The application form runs to twelve pages, and the clerk let me fill it in at home.
Critics panned the sequel when it came out. I assume the studio expected better reviews.
The collection is superb even though the building that houses it is modest.
Nobody at the meeting could say whether the slump in sales would last.
The recipe has more than twenty ingredients. My aunt let me copy the long list from her notebook.
The route is hard just because it gains a thousand metres in altitude.
The airline does not allow passengers to carry the extra weight on board.

notes: Card: top examples ' let' after 'But don't', ' though' after 'However, even', ' reason' after 'But neither…will be the main'. Probes: 'But don't let' 1.13, 'However, don't assume' 0.71, 'But do not allow the' 0.64, 'But just when you think' 0.56, 'Yet whether' 0.47; plain 'let'/'whether'/'Even though' without the opener <= 0.09. The - pole peaks on ' if', ' only', ' think' in 'even if', 'So if you think', 'not only': it may be the conceding side of the same contrast, not tested here.
